actualImplementation: Client.open first calls the SAME injected Vault.resume with the sealed original App material, binding the opaque namespace to the exact original identity without modifying the current CSR source. It then retains only bounded original bundle targets and a deterministic sorted-key bundle/group pin, not the whole resource tree.

Candidate and restored credentials convey no session capability. The real client must observe viewDeveloper plus listTeams; account DSID/personId/email stay pinned, the team comes from sealed original material and must be the one observed free Personal Team. Account/team changes reject overwrite and invalidate future credential use.

One reused ephemeral URLSession owner uses fixed HTTPS developer-services URLs, genuine default system server trust, no shared account cookies/cache/credential store, no interactive HTTP auth and no redirect forwarding. The actual response stream is bounded to the existing plist decoder limit and its owned task is cancelled on every exit.

Credential candidate and remote request intent reuse KeychainHelper only, under a dedicated random module namespace account/service, AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly and nonsynchronizable. Fresh OTP/anisette is not persisted. Logs/transport errors contain only fixed stage, byte counts and typed numeric codes; account, token, OTP, CSR subject and remote error text are not logged.

refreshMaterials calls the real same-Vault PKCS10 operation with namespace/keyID/expectedGeneration, serializes PEM according to the public original request, pins all original registered bundle IDs and dispatches the actual submitDevelopmentCSR/profile actions.

The returned real certificate public key is matched to the sealed CSR public hash. Final chain/date/key/profile double-CMS/team/prefix/AppID/ordered-group/entitlement checks and CAS publication all remain the original Vault.publish owner. A candidate certificate or external token cannot bypass it.

After all network awaits, account/team are re-observed and the current real key is reopened through another same-Vault CSR check; observed cancellation, stale generation or local revoke reject publication. Remote certificate OCSP/CRL and current Apple provisioning-purpose authority remain unimplemented.

A certificate-request intent is persisted BEFORE possible remote mutation. Uncertain/lost/cancelled ACK leaves it durable and prevents another automatic CSR/profile issue after restart. Original material stays intact on all prepublication failures; no fallback signer, certificate revocation, new App ID or group rewrite is introduced.

If Vault publication succeeds and later credential-journal clearing fails, PublicationFinalizationFailure carries the actual accepted lease. finalizeObservedPublication only re-reads/verifies that same real key/generation/certificate from the existing Vault and clears its pending intent; it performs no new remote request.

Logout requires the caller to cancel/await an active refresh, refusing busy rather than claiming atomic logout against another actor's pending Vault commit. Signed-out or invalidated in-memory credentials stay unusable even if the Keychain invalidation write fails; that error retains both session and storage failures.

independentRootReview.scope: Full two production files and eight native method definitions, current Vault/Keychain APIs, v1-to-v2 terminal event repair, pinned original account/team/profile wire facts. Source review only.
reviewedInvariants: Real Vault.resume binds namespace to sealed original material before client retention. Team and original bundle targets derive from that material; candidate/imported tokens never act as authorization capabilities.

Every observe/refresh actually invokes fixed developer-services viewDeveloper/listTeams with fresh anisette; pinned account/team mismatch, expiry and Keychain errors remain typed. Credentials and intent use only the existing namespaced Keychain helper with no book Cookie owner reuse.

One busy actor owns network awaits. Certificate intent is stored before dispatch, unknown/lost ACK remains pending across restart, and no blind resend, remote revoke or caller success reset is implemented.

Actual permanent-key CSR and returned public-key hash precede profiles; the same Vault validates chain, both signed profile CMS layers, original identity/groups and generation before its sole publish.
After acknowledged Vault publish, a later account save error retains the actual lease. Read-only finalization reopens the exact current key/generation/certificate and never repeats remote requests.

Transport reuses one ephemeral session, disables cookie/cache/shared credential storage, refuses redirects/interactive auth, preserves real system TLS trust, consumes bounded bytes and cancels the actual task on all exits. Errors expose stage/status integers rather than body/token/anisette.

The v1 test waiter could miss a pre-CSR refresh failure. V2 waits for the first actual CSR or refresh terminal event and observes the original task error, with parent cancellation reaching that task; it adds no sleep, queue or new test identity.

actualSourceCorrection: The actual refresh Task reports refreshFinished on both success and thrown failure/cancellation. The peer retains and delivers the FIRST actual CSR arrival or task-terminal event.

If the task-terminal event arrives first, the test awaits the ORIGINAL task.value, propagating its actual error into fixture cleanup; an unexpected early success records a failure and returns through normal cleanup.

If CSR arrives first, the existing cancellation/actual task.value assertions remain unchanged. Cancellation of the waiting parent cancels the real refresh task, whose real terminal callback releases the peer wait.
The event value is not signing/network proof. There is no new task queue, network connection, settle sleep, fake CSR success or extra behavior-test method.

limitsAndUnfinished: The three files are now committed, source-reviewed implementation. The actual client is not yet retained/called by AppSession/DI/UI and is not user-facing availability.

GSA SRP-6a init/complete, s2k/s2k_fo password KDF, M2/negotiated HMAC verification, authenticated SPD/app-token decryption, 2FA/device/SMS verification, token expiry/renewal and anisette generation/provisioning remain required implementation, not permanently blocked.

The current API accepts an explicit candidate app token only as transitional input and actually validates it remotely; there is no implemented producer of a real token yet. No fake token, paid API or controlled peer is counted as real authorization.

Issuer-chain bytes are explicit caller configuration for the existing Vault policy. Official intermediate acquisition/rotation, true Apple provisioning-purpose/entitlement and remote certificate revocation policy remain unaccepted; generic owned anchors are test trust only.

Only existing original registered App IDs are supported. Fresh/expired Personal Team AppID/device registration and required original groups/capabilities must be implemented without renaming the App; current absence or changed signed allowance fails closed.

Certificate-only key binding does not establish trust. The chain/profile validator must pass in the final actual Vault publication. Legacy certContent DER and encodedProfile Data are implemented; other currently deployed wire encodings need primary evidence and actual controlled checks before broader claims.

Unknown certificate-request outcome is conservatively pending even for a later definitive portal rejection. A full certificate-list/revoke-state reconciliation flow and bounded retry/backoff are unfinished; the current code intentionally provides no reset-success Boolean or blind retry.

Credential load/compare/save detects observed changes in this one injected actor; it is not cross-process atomic CAS. The existing App lifetime/flock owner must be wired before concurrent production exposure.

Per actual URLSession request/resource deadlines are30s and response limits1MiB. There is no infinite retry. The fresh-anisette provider is an injected unfinished dependency and must itself implement cancellation/deadline; no hard bound on an uncooperative provider is claimed.
No real account, current-server compatibility, free-team install/replacement, unattended renewal, cold userdata preservation or legal redistribution acceptance is established.

The controlled peer definitions use an outer Task.detached fixture; cancellation forwarding is only established by source for the waiting fixture scope, not an executed guarantee that SwiftTesting outer cancellation cancels every fixture child.
